sections.content: Practice question about secrets.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which value should generally never use the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: A database password is secret and should never intentionally be exposed to browser-side code.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 34
sections.content: Practice question about client JavaScript.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why can minimizing Client Components improve performance?
options: It can reduce browser JavaScript and client-side work
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Keeping more UI on the server can reduce the amount of JavaScript that must be downloaded, parsed, and executed in the browser.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 35
sections.content: Practice question about waterfalls.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which pattern can create an unnecessary request waterfall?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Sequentially awaiting unrelated operations forces later work to wait unnecessarily for earlier work.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 36
sections.content: Practice question about lazy loading.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which component is a strong candidate for lazy loading?
options: A large charting library used only on an analytics page
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Large, non-critical libraries can be loaded only when required to reduce initial client work.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 37
sections.content: Practice question about images.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why should large images be optimized?
options: Images can be among the largest resources transferred to users
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Images can consume significant bandwidth and affect loading metrics, especially on mobile networks.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 38
sections.content: Practice question about layout shift.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which practice helps reduce layout shifts caused by images?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Reserving the required space prevents content from jumping when an image finishes loading.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 39
sections.content: Practice question about production builds.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why should a production build be tested before deployment?
options: Development and production behavior are always identical
Production builds can expose configuration and build-time problems
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Production builds exercise optimizations and build-time processing that may not occur in the same way during development.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 40
sections.content: Practice question about horizontal scaling.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is a common requirement for horizontally scaled application servers?
options: All user state must live in one process's memory
Shared application state should not depend on one process
The database must run inside the browser
Every request must use the same server forever
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Requests may reach different instances, so important shared state should be stored in appropriate shared infrastructure.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 41
sections.content: Practice question about observability.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the purpose of a request ID?
options: To correlate activity belonging to one request across logs and services
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Correlation IDs allow engineers to trace one request across logs, services, and infrastructure.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 42
sections.content: Practice question about database performance.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which issue can significantly slow a data-heavy Next.js page?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: N+1 queries can cause a large number of database round trips and severely increase server latency.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 43
sections.content: Practice question about migrations.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why are backwards-compatible database migrations useful during deployments?
options: They ensure old and new application versions can coexist temporarily
They eliminate the need for databases
They force every server to restart simultaneously
interactiveQuiz.explanation: During rolling deployments, old and new application versions may run simultaneously. Compatible schema transitions reduce deployment risk.

sections.title: Performance & Production — Question 44
sections.content: Practice question about production debugging.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is generally the best first step during a production incident?
options: Identify the observable symptoms and scope of the failure
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Understanding when, where, and how broadly the problem occurs helps narrow the root cause before making risky changes.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 45
sections.content: Senior-level architecture scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A product page needs database data and has one interactive Add to Cart button. What is generally the strongest architecture?
options: Make the entire page a Client Component
Render product data on the server and isolate the button as a Client Component
Fetch the product only after browser hydration
Put the database query inside the button
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The product page can remain server-rendered while only the interactive button becomes client-side. This preserves server-side data access and minimizes browser JavaScript.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 46
sections.content: Senior-level caching scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A product update succeeds but the product listing still shows the old name. What should you investigate first?
options: Whether the CSS file is too large
Which caching layer contains the stale result
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Stale data can originate from multiple cache layers. Identifying the layer responsible is more reliable than disabling all caching.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 47
sections.content: Senior-level authentication scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A cookie works on one subdomain but not another related subdomain. Which is the most relevant area to inspect?
options: Cookie Domain, Path, Secure, and SameSite attributes
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Cross-subdomain cookie behavior is governed by browser cookie attributes and security policies, especially Domain and SameSite.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 48
sections.content: Senior-level performance scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A dashboard waits for three independent APIs before displaying anything. What is the most appropriate first optimization?
options: Parallelize independent requests and consider streaming their UI
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Independent requests can execute concurrently, and Suspense/streaming can allow faster portions of the interface to appear before slower data arrives.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 49
sections.content: Senior-level API architecture scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A Server Component needs data from your own database. Should you always create a Route Handler and call it over HTTP?
options: No, the Server Component can usually call a server-side data-access layer directly
interactiveQuiz.explanation: An internal HTTP hop is often unnecessary. Server Components can directly call server-side services or repositories.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 50
sections.content: Senior-level security scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A delete endpoint checks only whether a user is logged in. What security problem remains?
options: The user may still be unauthorized to delete the specific resource
The browser cannot send DELETE requests
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Authentication only establishes identity. The endpoint must also verify authorization, such as ownership or role permissions.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 51
sections.content: Senior-level Server Component scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why should `use client` not be added to the top-level page merely because one child needs state?
options: It can unnecessarily move a large portion of the tree into the client boundary
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The client boundary can increase browser JavaScript and remove opportunities for server-side execution. Isolate the interactive child when possible.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 52
sections.content: Senior-level hydration scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A component renders `Date.now()` directly during server rendering and also on the client. Why can this cause a hydration warning?
options: The server and client can produce different initial markup
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The server and browser can calculate different timestamps, causing their initial output to differ.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 53
sections.content: Senior-level webhook scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A payment provider sends the same webhook twice and your system creates two orders. What design principle is missing?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Webhook consumers should tolerate retries. An event identifier or equivalent idempotency mechanism can prevent duplicate business effects.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 54
sections.content: Senior-level architecture scenario.

interactiveQuiz.question: A team stores important shared session state in process memory while running ten application instances. What is the primary architectural problem?
options: Requests can reach different instances that do not have the same memory state
The browser automatically synchronizes server memory
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Process memory is local to one instance. Horizontally scaled systems generally need shared state infrastructure for state that must be available across instances.

sections.title: Senior Real-World Scenarios — Question 55
sections.content: Final expert architecture question.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the strongest general principle for designing a large Next.js application?
options: Make everything static regardless of requirements
Choose server/client execution, caching, data ownership, and rendering strategy based on the actual requirements of each feature
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Expert Next.js architecture is about making deliberate decisions. Server execution, client execution, caching, rendering, data access, and APIs should be selected according to security, freshness, interaction, performance, and maintainability requirements.
